name: AI for Literature Monitoring
blurb: Screening the scientific literature for safety reports.
title: AI for Literature Monitoring
answer: Companies must screen the literature for adverse events, and the volume keeps growing, more than 2.5 million scientific articles a year. AI screening can remove a large share of irrelevant articles while keeping almost all relevant ones; one proof of concept filtered out 55 percent of irrelevant articles while still capturing 99 percent of suspected adverse event reports.

reading.body:
AI screening can cut literature review workload without losing safety signals: one proof of concept removed 55 percent of irrelevant articles while capturing 99 percent of suspected adverse event reports.

The problem is volume. More than 2.5 million scientific articles are published each year, and that figure rose about 47 percent between 2016 and 2022. Companies are required to screen this literature for adverse events, so the input to the task grows while the obligation stays fixed.

The proof of concept points to where the leverage sits. Screening is a filtering problem, and filtering is what language models do cheaply at scale. The 55 percent reduction is real work removed from human reviewers, but the 99 percent recall figure is the one that governs deployment. A safety team should set the screening threshold for recall, not efficiency, because missing a report costs far more than reading an extra paper.

What the data does not cover is how either figure holds outside a single proof of concept. It gives no false negative count, no comparison against existing screening methods, and no evidence on whether performance persists as article volume keeps climbing. The two numbers describe one study, not a validated production system.

explainer:
Marketing authorisation holders must monitor the scientific literature for reports of adverse reactions to their products and treat qualifying articles as safety reports. With millions of articles published each year, most screening effort goes into reading articles that turn out to be irrelevant.

AI screening ranks or filters articles by how likely they are to contain a reportable case, so reviewers spend their time on the likely ones. The key design choice is the threshold: set for high recall, the system removes a large share of irrelevant articles while still passing through nearly all relevant ones. Because a missed case is a compliance and patient safety failure, systems are validated on how few relevant articles they miss, and the threshold is reviewed as literature patterns change.
